Compute cross-correlation between two neurons

Source: R/neuronsDG.R
compute.crosscorr.Rd

Computes the cross-correlation (raw or Pearson) between a reference neuron's spike train and a lagged copy of a comparison neuron's spike train. It's a wrapper around the compute_crosscorrelation_R method of the neuron class.

Usage

compute.crosscorr(
  nrn,
  nrn_compare,
  bin_count_action = "sum",
  max_lag,
  use_raw = TRUE,
  verbose = FALSE
)

Arguments

nrn

Reference neuron object.

nrn_compare

Comparison neuron object; must have trial length at least as long as nrn's.

bin_count_action

Method for counting spikes in each bin; one of "boolean", "mean", or "sum" (default: "sum").

max_lag

Maximum lag (in units of the trial data) to compute cross-correlation for.

use_raw

Logical indicating whether to use raw cross-correlation (true) or standard centered and normalized correlation (false) (default: TRUE).

verbose

Logical indicating whether to print progress information (default: FALSE).

Value

A numeric vector of cross-correlation values at lags from zero to max_lag.

Examples

raster_df <- data.frame(
  cell       = c(1, 1, 1, 1, 2, 2, 2, 2),
  time_in_ms = c(10, 20, 30, 40, 12, 22, 32, 42),
  trial      = c(1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1)
)
neurons <- load.rasters.as.neurons(raster_df, bin_size = 1)
compute.crosscorr(neurons[["neuron_1"]], neurons[["neuron_2"]], max_lag = 5)
#> [1] 0.09230769 0.00000000 0.00000000 0.00000000 0.00000000
